newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products--USG gasoline fades in quiet talk.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products--USG gasoline fades in quiet talk.

text.p: U.S. Gulf spot conventional gasoline differentials slipped lower by the end of trading Thursday, offsetting the gains made on the NYMEX.
New York Harbor heating oil differentials firmed modestly, while little change was noted in the quiet Midcontinent.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline gained 0.54 cent to settle at 57.08 cents and July heating oil gained 0.10 cent to finish at 51.62 cents.
U.S. GULF
Prompt conventional M1 gasoline differentials extended the drop seen early in the day as buyers backed out of the market following a scheduling deadline on the Colonial Pipeline Wednesday.
Conventional M1 differentials fell back between 2.25 and 2.50 cents under the July NYMEX, nearly 1.00 cent down from the levels seen late Wednesday, according to traders.

Active short covering at the scheduline deadlines for the Colonial, the main artery from Houston's "Refinery Row" to the East Coast, has driven differentials up several times in the past few weeks, though the strength has seldom lasted more than a day or two, traders said.
Prompt low sulphur 55-grade jet fuel firmed Thursday, with offers rising to even with the July NYMEX from 0.20 cent under the previous day.
NEW YORK HARBOR

Heating oil was bid stronger in the Harbor as a contango in the NYMEX futures spread provided an incentive to store the petroleum product and sell it at the more expensive price it has acquired in the later months.
"The widening contango just makes buying for storage perfect sense right now," said a U.S. Gulf trader.
Prompt heating oil was talked between 0.25 and 0.10 cent under July heat versus 0.75 and 0.50 cent under Wednesday.
Other distillates which trade at a differential to NYMEX heat also remained firm like low sulphur and jet fuel, dealers said.

Low sulphur diesel traded at 0.65 cent over in line with Wednesday's values of 0.45 to 0.70 cent over July heat. Prompt airline quality 54 grade jet fuel was talked in line with Wednesday's values of 1.25 to 1.50 cents over the July heat.
Meanwhile, reformulated gasoline failed generate much buying interest, holding to its weak differentials of 0.25 cent under to even with July heat.
MIDCONTINENT
Action remained subdued in midcontinent markets, notwithstanding vague unconfirmed talk that one refiner in the region was having processing problems.
Still the firming trend in Chicago unleaded markets was fortified amid talk of a deal for prompt barrels done at 4.40 cents over July NYMEX.
Firmness in the region was linked to continuing delays on the Explorer Pipeline system.
Explorer has said its 17th cycle June barrels will be delayed until July 1st or 2nd, instead of arriving Tulsa, Oklahoma, on June 22nd.

Differentials in Group Three unleaded markets held steady at 6.00/6.25 cents over July NYMEX, after gaining about a half cent on Wednesday. Any month barrels were up a half cent to 4.00 cents, with the 4.00 cent traded.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
